citation.quote:
OrderNotificationService computes the preview discount shown in the confirmation e-mail on purpose.
The e-mail shows an estimate; the binding discount is computed in the ordering domain at invoicing.
This is an accepted exception to keeping pricing rules in the domain layer.

exceptionClaim.scope: Only the preview (estimate) discount computed in OrderNotificationService for the order-confirmation e-mail. The binding discount at invoicing must still be computed in the ordering domain.

response.explanation: At line 9, OrderNotificationService.sendConfirmation in the notifications application layer applies a pricing rule: a 10% discount when the order has more than 3 lines. At line 10 it subtracts that discount from Order.subtotal() to get a payable amount. Discount and payable-amount rules naturally belong in the ordering domain, so SEM-MISPLACED flags this pricing rule in a notification service. The graph supports this reading: the service reads only the subtotal from the domain (CALLS Order.subtotal) and computes the rest itself. ADR-0003 (Status: Accepted) records this placement as a deliberate decision. The service computes a preview discount for the confirmation e-mail, while the binding discount is computed in the ordering domain at invoicing. Line 9 of the ADR calls this an accepted exception to keeping pricing rules in the domain layer. One gap between code and ADR: the ADR calls the figure an estimate, but line 11 sends it as "you pay X" with no estimate label. Also, the preview rule can drift away from the binding domain rule over time. The verdict stays a blocking fail.
